One other thing I will recommend; for Mint and Ubuntu, there's usually an article (or several) floating around out there with a title like: "top 10 things to do after you install (OS)". A lot of these articles contain a lot of stupid crap that you may or may not care about or may or may not be a good idea to install. On the other hand, if you're in a "learning how to linux" mode - a lot of these things are fun small projects, that teach you critical skills in how to manipulate various aspects of the system. So they're good, low-impact learning exercises, if nothing else.

Just know that; for some things, you may end up borking your system, or configuring it in a way you end up disliking. (in my case, when I was going through this process, I ended up breaking my package manager a couple of times, and also my desktop environment, when I tried tweaking gnome a bit too much. . . . good times). There are ways to fix these problems, of course, but you can always just blow away your system and reinstall. Both Ubutnu and Mint make this VERY easy and fast.
Even if you are too timid to make the changs in those articles, you should definitely read them because they will give you some good perspective.
